chapter: Opening and the Budweiser Dance Hall
title: Retiring from music in 1942: the Budweiser Dance Hall band
summary: Rene says he became a minister in 1939 and retired from music in 1942 from the Budweiser Dance Hall, naming Austin Young, Handy, Duke Deconje on piano and a guitarist, and how the pianist was killed.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: I've been a minister since 39. When I was old, Danny, in 39. I see. And I retired in music in the 1942's when I retired. From John Dennis Alvin Station. And that was from the Budweiser Dance Hall when I retired. Oh, yeah. Yeah. All those jobs, they were just...
Who else was working with you there?
Well, we had a brother, a fellow by the name, Sport Young. Oh, yeah.
Austin Young and his brother. They played the trambone. Saxophone. Or the sport saxophone. Yeah, well he had a brother who played the trambone too.
I heard Austin there in 1942 too.

Austin, yeah, yeah. And then Handy. What was he playing? Bass. His brother was playing bass. Eddie Hand, no Eddie Hand is the saxophone player. You see John Handy is the bass player. John Handy is the bass player, yeah.
No, John Handy played saxophone and clarinet. Yeah, that's right. And the bass player, Sylvester.

But he played a while there with us. And also Duke Deconje played the piano. And Butler rap. Gaillet. Gaillet, yeah. He played the guitar. And I played the drum. Duke Deconje? Duke Deconje, yeah. He played the piano with us. Does he play any other instruments? No, he just played none of the piano. He got killed. You know he had a shoe shop there on Ramport near Common and he went out with this this fellow played the piano, Richardson they called him. Herbert Richardson, you know Herbert Richardson? No? Well he went out one time to get some shoe business and he had a little food and he got in a wreck. He got killed. Now that's why we just used this fellow they called Walter Decon when I was the last one. So we had a little scrummage up there, you see. And after the scrummage let's see who we got to play the piano. Let's see if I can think who we had to play the piano.
He must have had a different guitar player too after that. Yeah we did.
Well I don't know about the place since this opened so long after that I think.
